newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota budget on track despite spring floods.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota budget on track despite spring floods.

text.p: North Dakota's budget has remained on track and slightly ahead of expectations despite a harsh winter, massive spring flooding in the east and drought conditions in some western areas, the state's budget director said Tuesday.
"We are actually doing somewhat better than projected," said Rod Backman, director of the office of management and budget.
"I would attribute that to the economy as a whole doing so well and the reconstruction activity in the Red River valley and Grand Forks happening faster than expected," Backman said.
Economic advisers told state officials that in other states disasters of the magnitude of the flooding actually brought some net economic benefits in the long run, Backman said.

Based on those reports, North Dakota expected to see a decline in the second quarter of the year because of the flooding, but it actually ran ahead of pre-flood projections because of rapid rebuilding efforts, Backman said.
The reconstruction has generated enough activity to cover losses in the cattle industry caused by the severe winter and flooding, Backman said.

North Dakota closed the last fiscal biennium with a $7 million higher surplus than projected in pre-flooding estimates, Backman said. The surplus reached $79 million, allowing the state to deposit $14 million in a state bank that provides budget stability, he said.
